name: horizon
description: How to work inside an Archon Horizon workspace — orient from on-disk state, pick the highest-value formalization work, record progress as commits, and coordinate. Load this first; it points to the specialized skills for detail. Editable per workspace.
---

You are working inside an **Archon Horizon** workspace: a place where AI agents
formalize mathematics in Lean 4 across one or more projects. This skill is the
map. It is deliberately short and **you can edit it** (it lives at
`.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` in this workspace) — tune it to how you want to
work. It points to focused skills; load those on demand rather than up front.

## You are a team; the workspace is where teams collaborate

Think of your session as **one team**: you (the lead) plus the subagents you
spawn as your **workers**, with the tools and skills available to you. A
`horizon run` is your team working through its task. Other runs are **other
teams** working in parallel on the *same shared workspace* — one Lean project set,
one roadmap/board, one ledger, one inbox.

You do not manage other teams and they do not manage you. You coordinate through
**shared state**, not meetings:

- **The board (roadmap)** is the shared plan. Keep your items' status/owner/
  milestone current so other teams see what you hold and where it's going.
- **The inbox** is asynchronous messaging + memory across teams (skill:
  `horizon-inbox`): shared notes, per-task private items, and direct messages to
  another team.
- **Commits** are the durable record; reading recent ledger history tells you what
  other teams just produced (skill: `project-git`).

Before you start, be aware of who else is live (see "Is another run live" below).
A short **synchronizer** digest is printed to stderr at the start of your CLI
commands. Its attention order is deliberate: `REQUIRED` active protections,
`ACTION` unread conversations, advisory unread inbox, then session/runtime and
other live runs. Read it; it is how you stay aware without asking anyone. A new
conversation or reply invalidates the digest cache immediately. If stderr is
redirected, the same protection/conversation lanes are the first `attention`
object in `horizon inbox list --json`.

## Orient (pull state, don't assume it)

**Start here:** your prompt says nothing about who ran before you. Usually
somebody did — often minutes ago, often on this same task, and their report was
written for you. Skill: `horizon-start` — one cheap pass that works out which
situation you were launched into (fresh run, hand-off from the session that just
finished, resume after a crash, or outside a run) and what to read for each.

The workspace root is `$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT`; your shell may start in a member
project rather than at that root. The absolute path to this skill is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`. Live state is under
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/.archon-horizon/` and the manifest is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/config.yaml`. Read what you need, when you need it — via the
`horizon` CLI (invoke it as `"$HORIZON_BIN" …`):

- **Roadmap** — YOUR strategy sketch across *all* projects, kept as a nested
  outline. `"$HORIZON_BIN" roadmap list` renders the indented tree with per-parent
  progress (`active · 3/7 done`); `--focus <id>` shows one subtree, `--max-depth 0`
  the top level only. Structure it: nest sub-goals with `--parent`, keep your
  item's status/strategy current as you work. It doubles as the **project board**:
  set `--owner <team>` (who holds it), `--milestone <label>` (a free grouping tag,
  filter with `roadmap list --milestone <label>`), and pin concrete deliverables
  with `--pin-commit <sha>`. Roadmap commands print a **warning**
  when parent/child statuses disagree (all sub-items done but parent open, or a
  done parent with open children) — nothing is auto-corrected; you decide whether
  to fix it or leave it (it may be intentional). They also warn when too many
  milestones claim simultaneous `active` focus.
- **Tasks** — a specific piece of work, usually the one a human launched and is
  watching. `"$HORIZON_BIN" task …`. Task commands warn when the open queue grows
  beyond the advisory limit or a `running` status looks orphaned.
- **Inbox** — how teams talk across sessions and projects. Leave a note for the
  next session; read what past ones left. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox …` (skill:
  `horizon-inbox`). Items can be **owned by your task** (private, e.g. your team's
  memory) or **shared with everyone** (the default); read-state is per-team, so
  `inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue, and you can
  direct-message another team with `--to task:<id>`. Inbox commands warn when the
  open working set—especially `memory` and `info`—needs review.
- **Inbox attention order** — before edits, inspect all open `protection` items
  (standing constraints, whether read or unread), then open unread
  `conversation` items and reply or mark them read. Other kinds are advisory
  context. In an agent session an unqualified `inbox list` defaults to open items
  and sorts in this order; use an explicit status to audit history.
- **Conversation discipline** — use a conversation only when a reply/decision is
  expected. Search and reuse an open thread before starting one. Its initiator is
  a participant and owns closure: after consuming the answer, add a concise
  conclusion if needed and archive the thread. Reply to human-started threads but
  leave their closure to the human unless asked otherwise (skill: `horizon-inbox`).
- **Blueprint graph** — declaration dependencies and what's proved. `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …` (skill: `hgraph`).
  Each node is also an **hgraph** file with attached comments/reviews —
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` ranks what to prove next, and node-scoped failure memory
  goes on the node itself (skill: `hgraph`).
- **Memory** — durable facts/dead-ends live in the inbox: read with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --kind memory --json`, write with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body …`.
- **Usage** — your token/cost consumption this session and run, budget headroom,
  and recent rate-limit signals: `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json`. See
  "Pace yourself" below for how to act on it.

124	The Picard group `Pic(X)` of any scheme is canonically an abelian group

132	`Scheme.Modules.pullback` for the underlying multiplicativity).

135	quotient `Pic(C ×_k T) / π_T^* Pic(T)` inherits a canonical
136	abelian-group structure under which the quotient map is a surjective

====
`PicSharp.addCommGroup` lives on `Quotient (RelPicPresheaf.preimage_subgroup πC πT)`,
whose carrier setoid is the **iso-class** relation `Nonempty (L.carrier ≅ L'.carrier)` — i.e. the
**absolute** `Pic(C ×_S T)`. The blueprint (`lem:rel_pic_sharp_groupoid`, Kleiman §2 `df:Pfs`) asks
instead for the **relative** quotient `Pic(C ×_S T) / π_T^* Pic(T)`, the quotient by the subgroup
`H_T := im π_T^*`. This section builds that quotient directly as a coarser setoid
`relPicSetoid` on `LineBundle.OnProduct πC πT`, together with the abelian-group instance
`PicSharp.addCommGroup_via_tensorObj` on it.

**Relation (multiplicative form).** For `L L' : OnProduct πC πT` set
```
L ~ L'   ↔   ∃ N locally trivial on T,  L.carrier ≅ π_T^* N ⊗ L'.carrier,
```
where `π_T^* N = (LineBundle.pullbackAlongProjection πC πT N hN).carrier`. This is the left-coset
relation of `H_T := im π_T^*`. It is **equivalent** to the blueprint's `L ⊗ L'^{-1} ≅ π_T^* N`
(tensor both sides by `L'` / its inverse), but the multiplicative form avoids naming the tensor
inverse of `L'` in the *definition* — only the setoid-symmetry step consumes a tensor inverse (of
`N` on the base `T`, via `Modules.exists_tensorObj_inverse`). The blueprint statements
`lem:relpic_setoid_{refl,symm,trans}`, `lem:relpic_add_welldef` and `lem:pullback_inverse_iso`
are realized below in that multiplicative form. -/

/-- **The `H_T`-coset relation on `OnProduct πC πT`** (relative Picard, multiplicative form):
`L ~ L' ↔ ∃ N loc-triv on T, L.carrier ≅ π_T^* N ⊗ L'.carrier`. It encodes the
quotient `Pic(C ×_S T) / π_T^* Pic(T)` of `lem:rel_pic_sharp_groupoid`, and is coarser than the
absolute iso-class relation `RelPicPresheaf.preimage_subgroup`. -/
def relPicRel {S C T : Scheme.{u}} (πC : C ⟶ S) (πT : T ⟶ S)
    (L L' : LineBundle.OnProduct πC πT) : Prop :=
  ∃ (N : T.Modules) (hN : LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial N),
    Nonempty (L.carrier ≅
      Modules.tensorObj (LineBundle.pullbackAlongProjection πC πT N hN).carrier L'.carrier)

/-- An isomorphism of the underlying bundles implies the `H_T`-coset relation (take `N = 𝒪_T`):
the relative relation is coarser than the absolute iso-class relation. Used to
transport the abelian-group axioms from the absolute iso-class group. -/
theorem relPicRel_of_iso {S C T : Scheme.{u}} {πC : C ⟶ S} {πT : T ⟶ S}
    {L L' : LineBundle.OnProduct πC πT} (e : Nonempty (L.carrier ≅ L'.carrier)) :
    relPicRel πC πT L L' := by
  obtain ⟨e⟩ := e
  refine ⟨SheafOfModules.unit T.ringCatSheaf, isLocallyTrivial_unit, ⟨?_⟩⟩
  exact e ≪≫ (Modules.tensorObj_left_unitor L'.carrier).symm ≪≫
    Modules.tensorObjIsoOfIso (Modules.pullbackUnitIso (Limits.pullback.snd πC πT)).symm
      (Iso.refl L'.carrier)

/-- **Reflexivity of the `H_T`-relation** (blueprint `lem:relpic_setoid_refl`): `L ~ L`, witnessed
by `N = 𝒪_T` and the pullback–unit iso `π_T^* 𝒪_T ≅ 𝒪_{C×T}` plus the left unitor. -/
theorem relPicRel_refl {S C T : Scheme.{u}} (πC : C ⟶ S) (πT : T ⟶ S)
    (L : LineBundle.OnProduct πC πT) : relPicRel πC πT L L :=
  relPicRel_of_iso ⟨Iso.refl _⟩

/-- **Symmetry of the `H_T`-relation** (blueprint `lem:relpic_setoid_symm`): from `L ~ L'` (via `N`)
get `L' ~ L` (via the tensor inverse `N⁻¹` on `T`), using multiplicativity of `π_T^*`, the
pullback–unit iso, and `Modules.exists_tensorObj_inverse`. -/
theorem relPicRel_symm {S C T : Scheme.{u}} {πC : C ⟶ S} {πT : T ⟶ S}
    {L L' : LineBundle.OnProduct πC πT} (h : relPicRel πC πT L L') :
    relPicRel πC πT L' L := by
  obtain ⟨N, hN, ⟨e⟩⟩ := h
  obtain ⟨Ninv, hNinv, ⟨eN⟩⟩ := Modules.exists_tensorObj_inverse hN
  refine ⟨Ninv, hNinv, ⟨?_⟩⟩
  -- `tensorObj (π_T^*Ninv) L ≅ L'`, then take `.symm`.
  refine Iso.symm ?_
  refine Modules.tensorObjIsoOfIso (Iso.refl _) e ≪≫ ?_
  refine (Modules.tensorObj_assoc_iso
    (M := (LineBundle.pullbackAlongProjection πC πT Ninv hNinv).carrier)
    (N := (LineBundle.pullbackAlongProjection πC πT N hN).carrier) (P := L'.carrier)).symm ≪≫ ?_
  refine Modules.tensorObjIsoOfIso
    (Modules.pullbackTensorIsoOfLocallyTrivial (Limits.pullback.snd πC πT) Ninv N hNinv hN).symm
    (Iso.refl L'.carrier) ≪≫ ?_
  refine Modules.tensorObjIsoOfIso
    ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (Limits.pullback.snd πC πT)).mapIso
      (Modules.tensorObj_braiding Ninv N ≪≫ eN)) (Iso.refl L'.carrier) ≪≫ ?_
  exact Modules.tensorObjIsoOfIso (Modules.pullbackUnitIso (Limits.pullback.snd πC πT))
    (Iso.refl L'.carrier) ≪≫ Modules.tensorObj_left_unitor L'.carrier

/-- **Transitivity of the `H_T`-relation** (blueprint `lem:relpic_setoid_trans`): from `L ~ L'` (via
`N`) and `L' ~ L''` (via `N'`) get `L ~ L''` via `N ⊗ N'`, using the associator and
multiplicativity of `π_T^*`. -/
theorem relPicRel_trans {S C T : Scheme.{u}} {πC : C ⟶ S} {πT : T ⟶ S}
    {L L' L'' : LineBundle.OnProduct πC πT}

81	### Decision 2: Mathlib kernel idiom for `f : G → H` of group schemes
82	
83	- **Mathlib idiom**: No direct idiom. The category-theoretic shape
84	  ("kernel of a group-object morphism in a finite-limit category") is
85	  the pullback `pullback f (e_H ∘ !) : ker f ⟶ G`, where
86	  `e_H : 𝟙_C ⟶ H` is the identity of the target group object and
87	  `!` is the unique map to the terminal. Mathlib supports this
88	  IMPLICITLY via `CategoryTheory.Limits.HasPullbacks` on schemes, but
89	  does not package `GrpObj.ker` as a named construction.
90	  Closest precedents:
91	  - `MonoidHom.ker` (`Mathlib.Algebra.Group.Subgroup.Ker`): plain
92	    group homomorphism in Type, returns `Subgroup G`. Not applicable
93	    at scheme level.
94	  - `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.ker`
95	    (`Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.IdealSheaf.Basic`): kernel ideal
96	    sheaf of a scheme morphism, i.e. `Y.IdealSheafData` not a
97	    `Scheme`. A different concept (set-theoretic preimage of zero
98	    section, not the categorical fiber over the identity element).
99	  - `CategoryTheory.Limits.kernel`: requires `HasZeroMorphisms`, not
100	    applicable to `Scheme` or `Over (Spec k)`.
101	  - `MonoidHom.fiberEquivKer`: the categorical insight (kernel =
102	    fiber over identity), but in Type only.
103	- **Project's natural reframing**: The directive's "Pic⁰ := ker(deg)"
104	  framing is conceptual. The PRACTICAL construction is the
105	  degree-stratification:
106	  `PicScheme C = ∐_{d∈ℤ} Pic^d C` (Kleiman `ex:curves`), with
107	  `Pic⁰ := Pic^0` the degree-0 open-and-closed subscheme. This sidesteps
108	  the categorical-pullback definition entirely.
109	- **Gap**: NEEDS_MATHLIB_GAP_FILL (categorical `GrpObj.ker`) but with
110	  workaround: the degree-stratification gives the kernel directly,
111	  without invoking pullback-of-identity. The kernel is the union of
112	  connected components mapping to `0 ∈ ℤ`, and in the discrete
113	  codomain case this is just the preimage of an open-and-closed
114	  point.
115	- **Verdict**: **NEEDS_MATHLIB_GAP_FILL** for the abstract idiom, but
116	  not on the critical path: the project does not need to invoke a
117	  generic kernel construction, only the curve-specific
118	  decomposition. The "ker(deg)" framing in the directive should be
119	  read as a NAMING / MATHEMATICAL JUSTIFICATION for the degree-0
120	  component, not as a literal `kernel.lift` / `pullback.lift`
121	  invocation.
122	
123	## Confirmation of the equivalence "ker(deg) = identity component"
124	
125	### Kleiman §6, `ex:curves` (lines 4665–4681 of `references/kleiman-picard-src/kleiman-picard.tex`)
126	
127	> *Assume $X/S$ is locally projective over $S$ and flat, and its
128	> geometric fibers are integral curves. Given an integer $m$, let
129	> $\Pic^m_{X/S} \subset \Pic_{X/S}$ be the set of points representing
130	> invertible sheaves $\mathcal L$ of degree $m$. Show the $\Pic^m_{X/S}$
131	> are open and closed subschemes of finite type; show they are
132	> disjoint and cover; and show that forming them commutes with
133	> changing $S$.*
134	>
135	> *Show there is no abuse of notation: the fiber of $\Pic^0_{X/S}$
136	> over $s\in S$ is the connected component of $0\in\Pic_{X_s/k_s}$.
137	> Show there is no torsion: $\Pic^0_{X/S}=\Pic^\tau_{X/S}$. Show each
138	> $\Pic^m_{X/S}$ is an fppf-torsor under $\Pic^0_{X/S}$.*
139	
140	This is the **direct citation** for `ker(deg) = identity component` on
141	smooth proper geometrically integral curves: the degree-0 component IS
142	the connected component of the identity. The project's curve hypotheses
143	(`SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom + IsProper C.hom + GeometricallyIntegral C.hom`)
144	satisfy Kleiman's setup.
145	
146	### Milne III.1 (PDF p.~93 / book p.~87)
147	
148	> *Let $\Pic^r(C)$ be the set of divisor classes of degree $r$. For
149	> a fixed point $P_0$ on $C$, the map $[D]\mapsto[D+rP_0]:
150	> \Pic^0(C)\to\Pic^r(C)$ is a bijection **(both $\Pic^0(C)$ and
151	> $\Pic^r(C)$ are fibres of the map $\deg : \Pic(C)\to\Z$)**.*
152	
153	And p.~88:
154	> *We write $\Pic^0(C)$ for the group of isomorphism classes of
155	> invertible sheaves of degree zero on $C$.*
156	
157	This is the **textbook definition of `Pic⁰` for a curve**: kernel of
158	the degree map. Milne's Theorem 1.6 then says this functor `P_C^0` is
159	represented by an abelian variety (the Jacobian), with no detour
160	through identity-component theory at all.
161	
162	### Kleiman §6 `rmk:curves` (line 4682)
163	
164	> *There is another important case where $\Pic^0_{X/S}=\Pic^\tau_{X/S}$,
165	> namely, when $X$ is an Abelian $S$-scheme. [...]*
166	
167	Confirms the identification also holds in the abelian-scheme case
168	(used downstream when iterating to `Pic⁰` of `Pic⁰`).
169	
170	**Conclusion**: The equivalence `ker(deg) = identity component` is
171	mathematically standard, explicitly cited in both primary sources
172	(Kleiman) and the project's secondary reference (Milne). For the
173	project's curve hypothesis it is provable from Kleiman §6 alone,
174	WITHOUT invoking 04KU / 04KV.
175	
176	## Recommendation
177	
178	**Pivot to ker(deg)-style Pic⁰ via the degree-stratification**, with
179	concrete plan:
180	
181	1. **Repurpose `IdentityComponent.lean`** (or split into two files).
182	   The abstract `GroupScheme.IdentityComponent` substrate can stay
183	   for future use (no urgency to close its sorries — those are
184	   pure-Mathlib upstream-grade lemmas).

187	   Sketch (using Mathlib b80f227 instances `inferInstance` shape):
188	   ```lean
189	   /-- Kleiman ex:curves: the degree-`d` component of the Picard scheme
190	   of a smooth proper geom integral curve, as an open-and-closed
191	   subscheme of `PicScheme C`. -/
192	   noncomputable def PicScheme.degComp {k : Type u} [Field k]
193	       (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
194	       [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
195	       [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom]
196	       (d : ℤ) : Over (Spec (.of k)) := ...
197	
198	   /-- The open-and-closed inclusion `Pic^d_{C/k} ↪ Pic_{C/k}`. -/
199	   noncomputable def PicScheme.degComp.ι {k : Type u} [Field k]
200	       (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [...] (d : ℤ) :
201	       PicScheme.degComp C d ⟶ PicScheme C := ...
202	   ```
203	
204	3. **Redefine `Pic0Scheme C := PicScheme.degComp C 0`** in
205	   `IdentityComponent.lean` (or new file `Picard/Pic0ByDegree.lean`).
206	   The TYPE remains `Over (Spec k)`, so downstream consumers in
207	   `Pic0AbelianVariety.lean` and `Albanese/AlbaneseUP.lean` are
208	   ABI-unchanged.
209	
210	4. **Inherit `GrpObj (Pic0Scheme C)`** from the multiplication on
211	   `PicScheme C`: `deg(L ⊗ M) = deg L + deg M`, so `Pic^0 × Pic^0 →
212	   Pic^0` via restricted multiplication. Closure under inverses:
213	   `deg(L⁻¹) = -deg L`, zero at degree 0. Identity: `O_C` has
214	   degree 0. Total LOC for the `GrpObj` instance: ~30–50.
215

217	   `Pic0.geometricallyIrreducible` in `Pic0AbelianVariety.lean`)
218	   STILL depends on identity-component theory in the long run
219	   (Kleiman `prp:pic0`), but with the pivot:

221	     its downstream `Pic^0`-torsor structure.
222	   - The substrate "`Pic^0` connected over `k̄`" can be deferred or

224	   - Or, in characteristic zero, derived from `Pic^τ` finiteness +

228	   theorem (currently captured loosely in

254	
255	- Identity-component path (parked): 4 iters elapsed at 0/it, ~350 LOC
256	  outstanding with substrate-unowned Mathlib gaps (Stacks 037Q,
257	  04KU/04KV). Best-case ~20+ iters; risk of unbounded park.
258	- Pivot path: ~6–10 iters (under Cartier route assumption for A.3.vii
259	  substrate ~3–5 iters + Pic⁰ assembly ~3–5 iters). Critical
260	  Mathlib gap is Hilbert-polynomial open-and-closed decomposition
261	  (Kleiman `thm:Pphifin`), which the project ALREADY plans to build
262	  for A.3.vii regardless.
263	
264	The pivot saves an estimated **10–18 iters** and removes the
265	unbounded-park risk on Stacks 04KU/04KV.

267	### Caveat — the geometric-irreducibility theorem still needs care
268	
269	`Pic0.geometricallyIrreducible` in `Pic0AbelianVariety.lean` is the
270	ONE downstream statement where the identity-component substrate
271	matters intrinsically: Kleiman `prp:pic0` proves
272	`Pic⁰ geometrically irreducible` precisely because it is the
273	connected component of the identity (in a smooth group scheme,
274	connected components are irreducible). Under the degree-stratification
275	definition, the geom-irreducibility of `Pic^0` is NOT immediate — it
276	still needs to be shown that `Pic^0` (= degree-0 component) is
277	connected, which IS the content of Stacks 04KU once you have a
278	section.

282	  `Pic⁰` or the bulk of downstream construction.
283	- It is needed only at the assembly stage (`Pic0.isAbelianVariety`),
284	  and can be attacked in isolation with the same Stacks 04KU
285	  substrate (or finessed via `Pic^τ` finiteness in characteristic 0).
286	- The other three conjuncts of "abelian variety" (smooth, proper,
287	  `GrpObj`) are independent and proceed via the pivot definition.
288	
289	This is a partial decoupling, not a full elimination. But it converts
290	the Stacks 04KU dependency from "blocks the whole positive-genus
291	arm" to "blocks one of four conjuncts of the assembly statement",
292	which is a strict improvement.
293	
294	### When the pivot might be wrong
295	
296	The pivot would be REJECTED if:
297	- Downstream consumers depend on `Pic0Scheme` being defined as
298	  `IdentityComponent (PicScheme C)` ABI (none do — confirmed by
299	  reading `Pic0AbelianVariety.lean` and `Albanese/AlbaneseUP.lean`).

303	- Mathlib were to ship 04KU/04KV imminently (low probability —
